answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, an agent network surveying a glacier, ferrous deposit, or onyx vein can deploy graph-theoretic trust routing. Agents certify bilateral edges based on reciprocal transactional histories, bounding collective flow through topological cuts. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of establishing genuine trust relationships with honest peers to cross network bottlenecks. However, this structure inherently disadvantages legitimate newcomer agents that lack prior connectivity.
